notes:
Summary: Cedarbridge builds a contract intelligence product for corporate legal teams. They're evaluating Redwood to power a RAG search experience across contracts, NDAs, and regulatory filings. Primary focus: embeddings + reranking pipeline economics at scale and operational simplicity when using managed vector DBs.

Key metrics / targets:
- Target index scale: 10M-50M vectors (2048-dim candidate embeddings), peak query load ~1200 QPS across multi-tenant namespaces.
- Ingestion profile: bulk backfill 12M documents over 8 weeks, steady-state 50k vectors/day, real-time updates for redacted docs ~100/day.
- Latency SLO: candidate generation (ANN) P50 <30ms, P95 <120ms; end-to-end with synchronous cross-encoder rerank P95 <=300ms for high-priority routes; acceptable async fallback with cached rerank for <80ms UI responses.
- Cost target: blended vector search + rerank <= $0.01 per query; looking for Redwood guidance on batching and quantization to hit this.

Vector DB & connector expectations:
- Vendor experiments: Pinecone (managed), pgvector (db-native), Elastic (hybrid text+vec). They want a single connector abstraction from Redwood that can target multiple backends with config flags, not a bespoke adapter per vendor.
- Connector musts: resumable bulk upsert (checkpoint token), per-tenant namespaces, hybrid BM25 + vector blending (tunable weights), server-side metadata filters, soft-delete + tombstone handling, point-in-time snapshot export (for audit), schema migration tooling, and backpressure handling for spike ingestion.
- Operational features: ability to run local ann bench (recall@k) against each backend, metrics export (QPS, P50/P95 latencies), automated tuning suggestions (HNSW M/efConstruction/efSearch), and a compatibility matrix for quantized embeddings (int8/4-bit) vs reranker quality.

Rerank and model strategy:
- Candidate retrieval: ANN returns top-500 for rerank experiments (exploratory); baseline production will likely be top-100.
- Reranker options: cross-encoder fine-tuned on in-domain contract pairs; experiments planned on small-distil cross-encoder on CPU vs larger cross-encoder on Dedicated GPU. They want Redwood to propose the sweet spot (precision/latency/cost).
- Caching: top-k caching per query fingerprint + TTL, and KV cache for prompt/context to avoid recomputing embeddings for frequently updated clauses.

Quality & evaluation needs:
- Benchmark suite: 2k labeled query-doc pairs for recall/precision/rerank NDCG; business metric: time-to-first-relevant-doc for legal reviewers.
- Regression alerts: drift detection vs baseline eval set, automated rollback if quality drops >3% NDCG.

POC plan (agreed):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): connector smoke tests - bulk upsert 500k vectors to Pinecone and pgvector testbeds; validate idempotency and resumability.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): perf sweep - run candidate-gen bench at 1M, 5M, 10M shards; capture P50/P95 and memory usage; tune HNSW params and test quantized index profiles.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): rerank integration - deploy cross-encoder on Redwood Dedicated; measure end-to-end latency at 100 QPS and 1k QPS with batching; validate async fallback.
- Phase 4 (1 week): quality & cost report - NDCG comparisons, cost-per-query modeling, recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
